name: Modbus Controller
description: The `modbus_controller` component creates an RS485 connection to control a Modbus server (slave) device, letting your ESPHome node act as a Modbus client (master). You can access the coils, inputs, holding, read registers from your devices as sensors, switches, selects, numbers or various other ESPHome components and present them to your favorite Home Automation system. You can even write them as binary or float outputs from ESPHome.

config_entries.label: Address
config_entries.description: start address of the first register in a range (can be decimal or hexadecimal).

config_entries.label: Update Interval
config_entries.description: The interval that the sensors should be checked. Defaults to 60 seconds.

config_entries.label: Modbus ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID of the `modbus` hub.

config_entries.label: ID
config_entries.description: Manually specify the ID used for code generation.

config_entries.label: Continuous
config_entries.description: Poll as fast as the bus allows instead of once per update interval. Defaults to `false`. See [Continuous polling](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_controller#modbus_controller-continuous-polling) below.

config_entries.label: Max Cmd Retries
config_entries.description: How many times a command will be retried if no response is received. It doesn't include the initial transmission. Defaults to 4.

config_entries.label: Offline Skip Updates
config_entries.description: How many update intervals to wait between retry attempts while a device is offline (see below). Defaults to `0` (retry every update interval). If using a bus with multiple slaves, this avoids waiting for timeouts on an unresponsive device, allowing the other slaves on the same bus to be read on time.
